steps: 1. App opens on Home, already populated from bundled fixtures | 2. One background fetch replaces that with server data (status, P&L, positions, decisions, risk) | 3. User reads the four dashboard questions in their numbered order
branches: Server unreachable: fixtures stay on screen, freshness line still reads 42s, and nothing says the fetch failed (logged only)
end_state: User has an answer to 'does anything need me?', or leaves
review_focus: Reading order of the four numbered sections; whether the circled section numbers are announced; the all-caps section titles

steps: 1. Tap a bottom-nav slot | 2. That section renders and the slot marks itself selected (top rule, filled glyph, semibold label)
branches: Tapping Positions while in Position detail returns to the board, not the detail screen
review_focus: Glyphs are deliberately empty bordered squares, so labels carry the entire meaning; selection conveyed by weight and fill; slots set no role or selected-state semantics

steps: 1. Tap the 'P&L: FLOOR' chip | 2. It cycles FLOOR to POLICY to MID to FLOOR | 3. Every money figure on that screen re-renders and the trailing band labels update with it
branches: Band is per-screen state: leaving the section and coming back resets it to FLOOR | Risk shows money with no chip on the screen to relabel it
end_state: Screen shows figures in the chosen band
controls: Band chip (Role.Button, onClickLabel 'Change which P&L band is shown')
review_focus: A cycling control that never shows its full set of states, and whose only feedback is the numbers silently changing

flow_name: Check freshness, or notice the engine is paused
steps: 1. Read the chrome strip under the app bar | 2. If paused, a dot and the line 'New entries paused. The engine is still managing exits.' sit above the freshness figure
end_state: User knows the data age and whether entries are paused
review_focus: No pull-to-refresh, manual refresh, or polling: the data age shown is whatever the single startup fetch returned and it does not advance

entry_point: Launch, or nav to Home, with nothing pending
steps: 1. Read the 'Nothing needs you' strip and the next check time | 2. Read P&L across the four windows: today, week, month, year | 3. Read capital deployed against idle | 4. Read the four position quick-rows, then leave
end_state: No action taken. The intended everyday flow
review_focus: Quiet-state reading order; the check-mark glyph carries no text alternative

entry_point: Home with at least one pending card
steps: 1. Read the card header: type label, action, sub-line, deadline chip | 2. Read the headline figure: annualized percent against the APR gate | 3. Read the key-value grid: premium, IV rank, assignment odds | 4. Tap 'Why the engine wants this (5)' to expand the reasons list | 5. Collapse it again
branches: On the stop-trigger card the reasons are expanded by default, and an attribution split bar replaces the headline figure
end_state: User is informed; the card is still pending
review_focus: Disclosure uses text glyphs for its arrow and does carry an expand/collapse click label; the attribution split is colour-coded with the percentage also written out

steps: 1. Tap Approve, the filled primary-styled button | 2. The app posts the decision, then refetches everything | 3. The resolved card disappears from the list and the nav badge count drops
branches: Post fails: logged, no message, card stays exactly as it was
end_state: Card gone. That disappearance is the only success signal
flags: writes to server; no confirm; no in-flight state; silent failure
review_focus: A money-moving action taken in one tap, with no confirmation, no in-flight state, and an outcome announced entirely by content vanishing from the list

flow_name: Veto a proposal, with a reason
entry_point: Veto on an entry card, or Hold on a stop-trigger card (both are rejections; both route here)
steps: 1. Tap Veto or Hold: a modal bottom sheet slides up over the screen, with a drag handle and a scrim | 2. Read the title 'Why veto this?' and the note explaining that this text is what trains the rubric | 3. Focus the single free-text field (placeholder 'What did the engine miss?'); the soft keyboard opens over the sheet | 4. Type a reason. Confirm veto is disabled while the field is blank and enables on the first non-space character | 5. Tap Confirm veto: sheet dismisses, post with the reason, refresh, card disappears
branches: Tap Cancel: abandons, text discarded | Tap the scrim: abandons, text discarded | System back: abandons, text discarded | Drag the sheet down: abandons, text discarded. Reopening always starts empty | Post fails: logged, no message, the card stays exactly as it was
end_state: Card gone and the reason posted, or the veto abandoned with input lost
controls: Veto / Hold button; reason text field; Confirm veto (disabled until non-blank); Cancel; drag handle; scrim
flags: form; modal; label mismatch; input loss on dismiss; silent failure
review_focus: The only form in the app: focus movement into and out of the modal, keyboard occlusion of the Confirm/Cancel row, a disabled-until-valid button dimmed to 40% with no stated reason, and four separate dismissals that discard typed input. The sheet says 'veto' even when the Hold button opened it

entry_point: Home, any card carrying a Snooze option
steps: 1. Tap Snooze, ghost-styled and narrower than its siblings | 2. Immediate post, then refresh; the card leaves the list
branches: Post fails: logged, no message, the card stays exactly as it was
flags: writes to server; no confirm; no undo; silent failure
review_focus: No confirmation, no undo, and no indication of how long a snooze lasts

entry_point: Home, stop-trigger card: the stop was hit, but the adverse move is volatility-driven rather than the stock sliding
steps: 1. Read the reasons, which are already expanded on this card type | 2. Read the attribution split: how much of the move is the stock and how much is volatility | 3. Choose Exit now, Hold, or Snooze
branches: Exit now: single tap, shaped like H3 | Hold: opens the reason sheet, H4 | Snooze: H5 | Post fails: logged, no message, the card stays exactly as it was
flags: writes to server; colour-carried meaning; no default option; silent failure
review_focus: The hold-versus-exit judgment rests entirely on the attribution split, drawn as a tinted bar plus text. Deadline chip is warn-tinted on this card type. No button is primary-styled, since the engine is escalating a conflict rather than recommending

steps: 1. Read the realized loss and its attribution | 2. Read three branch rows: each a radio glyph, a label, and a one-line detail; one carries an ENGINE'S PICK tag | 3. Tap a row to select it. The row fills and its border thickens | 4. Confirm choice enables. Tap it: post, then refresh
branches: The selection can be changed any number of times before confirming | Nothing is pre-selected, and the footnote says so: agreeing costs the same tap as disagreeing | Post fails: logged, no message, the card stays exactly as it was
controls: Three branch rows (Role.Button, onClickLabel = option label); Confirm choice (disabled until a row is selected)
flags: select then confirm; radio group without radio semantics; silent failure
review_focus: Behaviourally a radio group, but built as clickable rows with a button click-label: no selection semantics, no group semantics. Selected state is conveyed by fill, border weight, and a drawn dot

flow_name: Go from Home to the full board
steps: 1. Tap 'All' | 2. Nothing happens: the handler is never wired up
branches: The working path to the board is the bottom nav (G2) | 'Deadline order' on the question-1 header is a label only and is not clickable
review_focus: A clickable element with no effect; the adjacent 'Deadline order' reads as a link but is inert

steps: 1. Read three aggregate cells (margin, net exposure, synthetic cash), each a figure over a thin meter bar | 2. Read the section header: underlying count on the left, banded total on the right | 3. Read one row per underlying: contract identity and total P&L, then economics, then the engine's management line | 4. Read the closing note on which figures carry a band and which are facts
end_state: User knows the state of the book
controls: Rows are clickable (see P2 / P3); nothing else required
review_focus: Meaning is carried by wheel-stage dots, meter bars, exit-clock chips, a distance-to-strike bar, and a colour escalation (plain, then warn at 1.5x the credit, then alarm or volatility-tinted at 2x) alongside the text

flow_name: Drill into a position and come back
entry_point: Positions board, a row that has detail data (MSFT today)
steps: 1. Tap the row: Position detail for that ticker | 2. Read down: header, economics grid, stop meter, unrealized row, auto-exit note, volatility context from entry to now, P&L attribution split | 3. Read the position facts: stock price, distance to strike, delta, margin consumed, assignment odds | 4. System back or the back gesture returns to the board
branches: Bottom nav also exits the detail screen (G2) | The band chip works here, and is again independent of the board's
controls: Board row (Role.Button, onClickLabel 'Open MSFT detail'); system back; band chip
review_focus: There is no on-screen back affordance: the app bar holds only the ticker and the band chip. Back is handled, but only by the system control

flow_name: Tap a row that has no detail
entry_point: Positions board, any row other than MSFT
review_focus: Every row is clickable and every row announces 'Open TICKER detail', including the four that do not navigate

steps: 1. Read the 'if everything assigns at once' figure against available cash and margin | 2. Read the concentration bars by underlying | 3. Read the largest-name question line beneath them
end_state: User knows the standing worst-case exposure
review_focus: Money on this screen has no band chip anywhere on the screen to label which value it is

flow_name: Engage or release the kill switch
entry_point: Risk, kill-switch box at the bottom of the scroll
steps: 1. Read the copy: pausing stops the engine opening new positions, and it keeps managing exits (rolls, buy-backs, assignments continue) | 2. Tap Pause new entries | 3. The request round-trips; on success the button inverts to a filled Resume new entries | 4. The paused banner appears in the chrome of every screen
branches: Reverse: tap Resume new entries; the banner clears everywhere | Request fails: logged, the button does not change, no message | One tap arms it; there is no confirmation dialog, by requirement
end_state: Engine paused or resumed, and the global banner matches
controls: Kill switch button (Role.Button, onClickLabel 'Pause new entries' / 'Resume new entries', disabled while in flight)
flags: writes to server; no confirm; no in-flight state; silent failure
review_focus: The screen supports an in-flight state ('Pausing...', button disabled) but the host never passes the flag, so it never appears. Between tap and reply the button looks untouched
